open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text:
The same refusal answers a
   failure to open or lock the lock file, which waiting for another holder is not, and a mark that cannot be
   written.
open_points.question: Do the preceding guarantees that the operation changes no record and no stored image apply to lock-file failures and failed mark writes, or does this sentence carry forward only the STATE_UNAVAILABLE refusal code?
options: All listed STATE_UNAVAILABLE cases must change no record and no stored image.
Only the damaged-record case has the no-change guarantee; the later cases are guaranteed only to return STATE_UNAVAILABLE.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the no-change guarantee to every refusal listed in rule 5.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a publication mark.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to record a publication.
The deliverer begins writing the mark, but the write fails.
outcomes: The call returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE and leaves every record and stored image unchanged.
The call returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE, but partial mark-write effects may remain because only the refusal code was carried forward.
witness.observer: The calling flow and a later scan or mark call

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text:
Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and
   its folder is synchronised, so a reader sees a complete file or none.
open_points.question: When writing a mark reaches rename successfully but synchronising the folder then fails, is the mark considered written or unable to be written, what response is returned, and must the implementation remove or preserve the renamed record?
options: Return STATE_UNAVAILABLE and compensate by removing the renamed mark so no record changes.
Return STATE_UNAVAILABLE but leave the complete renamed mark in place.
Treat the rename as a successful mark despite the folder-synchronisation failure.
open_points.default_guess: Return STATE_UNAVAILABLE and attempt to restore the pre-call state, while specifying what happens if that compensation also fails.

witness.initial: A placement exists and no mark record exists.
events: The calling flow asks to record photo_id A.
The deliverer writes and synchronises a temporary mark file.
The deliverer renames it to the final mark path.
outcomes: The call is refused and the final mark is removed.
The call is refused but a later call finds the final mark.
The call reports marked and preserves the final mark.
witness.observer: The caller immediately, and any later scan, delivery, or mark call

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: INV-20: with a damaged placement or mark record, scan, delivery and mark each answer M08 with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode and the record stays as it was (`test_a_damaged_record_refuses_and_is_never_taken_for_an_absent_one`), and a mark that cannot be written is refused (`test_a_mark_that_cannot_be_written_is_refused`).
open_points.question: Must the INV-20 tests also show that every stored image remains unchanged, and must the failed-mark-write test show that no record changed, as required by the amended normative rule?
options: Snapshot and assert all relevant records and stored images are unchanged in both cases.
Assert only the damaged record is unchanged; the stored-image guarantee and failed-write side effects remain untested.
Create a separate formal invariant and Required tests item for the new no-change guarantee.
open_points.default_guess: Extend the formal invariant and its tests to assert that relevant records and all stored images remain unchanged.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text:
every
operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: What exactly makes an attempted operation an operation “on a project,” especially when the project identifier is malformed, unknown, or absent, and must authentication be checked before deciding that classification?
options: Every scan, delivery, and publication-mark attempt is project-scoped even when its project identifier is malformed or unknown, so the token is checked first.
An attempt is project-scoped only after a syntactically valid existing project is identified, so validation or lookup may precede authentication.
Each operation defines separately whether malformed or unknown project requests are project-scoped.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every invocation of the three project operations as project-scoped and check the token before project-id validation or lookup.

witness.initial: The caller has no valid token and supplies a malformed project identifier.
events: The caller invokes a project operation.
The service must choose whether to authenticate or classify and validate the project first.
outcomes: The service refuses the request at the token boundary without revealing project-id validity.
The service first returns a project-id or unknown-project refusal because the attempt was not yet considered an operation on a project.
